'''Louis Skurcenski, Jr.''' (January 29, 1943 – December 22, 1998) was born in Braddock, PA to the late Louis Skurcenski, Sr. and Margaret Hornick.<ref name="BCF">{{cite web |title=Lou Skurcenski Memorial Scholarship |url=http://bartlesvillecf.org/scholarships/lou-skurcenski-memorial-scholarship/ |accessdate=13 June 2017 |website=Bartlesville Community Foundation |ref=BCF}}</ref> He was an All-American college basketball player at [[Westminster College (Pennsylvania)|Westminster College]], playing 4 seasons from 1960 to 1964, including the 1962 team that was voted the No. 1 small college team in America. His career stats and records are impressive. In his 4 year career, he scored 1,182 points (#25 all time), 608 field goals (#3 all time), 20 rebounds in 1 game (tied for #6 all time), 289 rebounds in 1 season (#2 all time), and 958 career rebounds (#2 all time).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Lou Skurcenski memorial student/athlete scholarship Founded |url=https://bartlesvillecf.org/files/2022/04/0182_001.pdf}}</ref>

== Education ==
He graduated from Westminster in 1964 with a bachelor of science degree in chemistry, toured [[South America]] for four weeks on a Goodwill Tour sponsored by the [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]], and participated in the [[1964 Olympics|1964 Olympic]] Trials with 93 top collegiate, A.A.U. and Armed Forces players at St. John's Alumni Hall in Jamaica, Queens. Notable names who participated in the Olympic trials included [[Bill Bradley|Bill Bradly]], [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]], [[Walt Hazzard]], [[Lucious Jackson]] and head coach [[Henry Iba|Hank Iba]].<ref name=":0" />

== Family ==
He married Stephanie Solomon and had two children - Jason and Amy.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
He was drafted in the 5th round (40th overall pick) by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref name="RealGM">{{cite web |title=Lou Skurcenski |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Lou-Skurcenski/Summary/68896 |accessdate=13 June 2017 |website=RealGM |publisher=RealGM, L.L.C.}}</ref> After deciding not to continue playing for 76ers, he joined the Pittsburgh Pipers of the American Basketball Association (ABA) in 1967 to play with the likes of Connie Hawkins, Tom Kerwin, and Art Heyman. However, he was not offered a no cut contract so he moved back to Oklahoma to play for the [[Phillips 66ers]] in [[Bartlesville, Oklahoma]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bartlesville Examiner-Enterprise |url=https://www.examiner-enterprise.com/restricted/?return=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.examiner-enterprise.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Flocal%2F2022%2F07%2F13%2Fformer-phillips-66ers-player-lou-skurcenski-made-it-a-wonderful-life%2F65370226007%2F |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.examiner-enterprise.com}}</ref> He played with teammates such as Jim Kerwin, Bill Kusleika, Bobby Rascoe, and Darel Carrier. Lou worked in the Chemical Research Division of the [[Phillips Petroleum Company]] for 34 years before his retirement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-15 |title=Lou Skurcenski helped close out amazing Phillips 66ers legacy |url=https://news.yahoo.com/lou-skurcenski-helped-close-amazing-120928378.html |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref>

He received honors, including Westminster College Varsity "W" Athlete of the Year (1964) and induction into the Lawrence County Historical Society Hall of Fame (1996),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hall of Fame Inductees - Lawrence County Historical Society |url=https://www.lawrencechs.com/sports-hall-of-fame/hall-of-fame-inductees/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.lawrencechs.com}}</ref> Westminster College Sports Hall of Fame (1988)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lou Skurcenski (1988) - Titan Sports Hall of Fame |url=https://athletics.westminster.edu/hof.aspx?hof=249&path=&kiosk= |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Westminster College Athletics |language=en}}</ref> and the Bartlesville Sports Commission Hall of Fame (2023).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lou Skurcenski |url=http://bartlesvillesports.net/inductee/lou-skurcenski/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Bartlesville Sports Commission |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lou was a supporter of youth sports in Bartlesville and spent time as a coach, mentor, volunteer, and fan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bartlesville Examiner-Enterprise |url=https://www.examiner-enterprise.com/restricted/?return=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.examiner-enterprise.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Flocal%2F2022%2F07%2F12%2Fformer-bartlesville-phillips-66ers-basketball-player-lou-skurcenski-displayed-class%2F65370225007%2F |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.examiner-enterprise.com}}</ref> He tutored and encouraged students in the pursuit of science and business. Due to the generosity of family and friends to honor "Big Lou", memorial scholarships were established at Westminster College and [[Bartlesville High School]] to provide funds for students who embodied the qualities of a leader (integrity, good sportsmanship and a positive attitude) to further their education in college.<ref name=":0" />

== Death ==
Lou died of cancer in December 1998 at the age of 55 and his funeral was on December 24, 1998, in Bartlesville, Oklahoma. He received numerous honors, including induction into the Lawrence County Historical Society Hall of Fame (1996).
